definitions.gloss: musical accompaniment in traditional performing arts
definitions.explanation: The instrumental ensemble or musical accompaniment used in traditional Japanese performing arts such as Noh, Kabuki, and festival performances. Typically features flute and drums.

examples.japanese: {囃子|はやし}の{音|ね}が{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: I can hear the sound of the musical accompaniment.

examples.japanese: {能|のう}の{舞台|ぶたい}では{囃子|はやし}が{重要|じゅうよう}な{役割|やくわり}を{果|は}たす。
examples.english: In Noh performances, the musical accompaniment plays an important role.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{囃子|はやし}が{通|とお}りに{響|ひび}き{渡|わた}り、{子供|こども}たちが{駆|か}け{寄|よ}ってきた。
examples.english: The festival music echoed through the streets, and children came running over.

notes:
USAGE: {囃子|はやし} refers specifically to the instrumental ensemble in traditional Japanese performing arts. It is not used for Western-style musical accompaniment, which would be {伴奏|ばんそう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {囃子|はやし}の{音|ね} (sound of the accompaniment)
- {祭|まつ}り{囃子|ばやし} (festival music) — note the voicing: はやし → ばやし
- {能|のう}{囃子|ばやし} (Noh accompaniment)
- {囃子方|はやしかた} (musicians in the ensemble)

The standard Noh {囃子|はやし} ensemble consists of four instruments: {笛|ふえ} (flute), {小鼓|こつづみ} (small hand drum), {大鼓|おおつづみ} (large hand drum), and {太鼓|たいこ} (stick drum). In compounds, the reading often voices to ばやし (rendaku).
